metadata.title: Macular Drusen H&E
metadata.description: Histological section of the right eye of a 92 year old female donor with atrophic (early-intermediate) age-related macular degeneration (AMD) shows the presence of drusen beneath the retina pigment epithelium. Eyes were fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 hours followed by washing in PBS, infiltration in graded sucrose and embedment in sucrose-OCT. Sections collected at 7µm were stained with hematoxylin-eosin stain. Photomicrography was performed using an Olympus BX41 microscope with SPOT-RT digital camera using a 20x objective lens. Scalebar = 100µm

metadata.title: Supplementary data for: Abducens nerve palsy with ipsilateral excessive eye tearing attributed to internal carotid artery sympathetic plexus schwannoma
metadata.description:
A 65-year-old man developed subacute horizontal diplopia due to left-abducens nerve (AN) palsy and excessive left-eye tearing. Brain-MRI revealed a hyperintense T2-lesion with an elongated course within the left-carotid canal, presenting homogenous contrast-enhancement (Figure-1). The imaging findings were characteristic for an internal-carotid-artery sympathetic plexus (ICSP) schwannoma compressing the left-AN. Subsequent irritation of the deep petrosal nerve originating directly from ICSP and continuing as the vidian nerve may have led to the lacrimal gland edema and excessive left-eye tearing (Figure-2).

ICSP schwannoma represents an uncommon cause of AN palsy that may also manifest with excessive ipsilateral-eye tearing due to vidian nerve involvement.
